quote: I just got a Tesla. And as I was thinking about it, I was like, hey. What if I just charge this off of the sun? And then, you know, we got a huge roof line. You'll see it... it's, like, six or 7,000 square feet.
stewart_read: This is a double enthusiasm signal — a newly purchased EV (higher electric load, directly relevant to system sizing) and an unusually large roofline volunteered in the same breath. The rep captured the EV detail later for the design team but never explicitly reflected the roof-size comment back to the customer as a hook.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to briefly mirror standout details back ('a 6-7,000 square foot roof line is going to give the design team a lot to work with') — it costs seconds and reinforces the customer's own excitement rather than just filing it silently.

quote: the only requirement is that either of you guys has a credit score of 650 or higher.
stewart_read: Rep states 650 as the threshold, matching the same drift previously observed in SESSION18_fcbf33c1, while the schema's documented threshold is 670. This is a second instance of the same discrepancy, suggesting it may be a live floor-wide script variant rather than an isolated rep error.
coaching_implication: Flag to Kenny for reconciliation: is 650 the current active threshold, and does the schema need updating, or are reps drifting from 670? Two independent calls citing 650 makes this worth resolving rather than treating as noise.

quote: I have you here, Kyle, as the property owner. Is there anyone else on the title of the home with you at all?
stewart_read: Customer discloses the home is actually titled in his wife's name, a stronger co-owner signal than a typical spousal mention, and the rep's response was a brief acknowledgment ('No problem at all') without inviting her onto the appointment. Because the follow-up appointment is an in-person specialist visit at the home rather than a phone call, the risk here is more moderate than the phone-coordination scenario protocols.spouse_decision was built around — a specialist visiting the house has some natural opportunity to meet her regardless.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep should have asked whether the wife would be present for the in-home visit, matching protocol intent. Strategic read considered but not adopted: there's no evidence the rep deliberately deferred this to the closer/specialist — the line just moves straight to utility questions with no bridge.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to add one line confirming the wife's availability for the specialist's visit, especially since she is the titled owner — a small addition that closes an open gap without needing to treat it as a phone-scheduling protocol violation.

quote: No. Actually, I've got something tomorrow.
stewart_read: What started as a same-week booking opportunity (specialist available in the area the next day) unwound into three separate date changes before landing nearly two weeks out on Friday the 7th. The rep didn't push back or offer an earlier alternative before Friday's week, simply following the customer's drift.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read considered: rep may have judged that pushing a firm near-term date against a clearly busy schedule risked losing the booking entirely, so ceding to the customer's preferred window was the safer play. This is the better-supported read given the rep never argues and simply adapts.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep on tightening the reconfirm commitment given the length of the gap — the general 'we'll call or text Thursday the sixth' line is good practice, but a specific ask like 'does 12pm still work best given your schedule right now?' would test durability before locking it in.

quote: That's exactly what we'll be able to show you once we kinda get this built up.
stewart_read: This is actually the escape hatch working correctly — customer asks about cost and investment timeline, and rep redirects to the design team rather than estimating numbers himself. Included here as a positive marker, not a violation.
coaching_implication: Reinforce this as the model move for this rep — redirecting a pricing question cleanly without fabricating a range is exactly what setter_scope_discipline calls for.

quote: 4,000 kilowatt hours is there after the year. I think we're paying, like, 15¢ kilowatt hours, so 500 something bucks, 600.
stewart_read: Customer gives a specific bill figure ($500-600/month) unprompted alongside usage detail. Rep acknowledges and moves straight into the seasonal-variance follow-up without ever reflecting the number back as pain or leverage.
coaching_implication: This is the clearest missed flip on the call — a $500-600 bill is a strong anchor, and a line like 'so we're looking at a pretty significant bill to offset there' would have planted the emotional hook the schema calls for.
